subject: biology-1
question: During **anaphase I** of meiosis in a diploid cell, a student observes chromosomes moving toward opposite poles. Which description matches what is actually separating at this stage?

options.text: Homologous chromosomes are being pulled to opposite poles, while sister chromatids stay together.
Sister chromatids are being pulled apart toward opposite poles.
The four chromatids of each tetrad are distributing one to each of four poles.
Chromosomes have finished separating and new nuclear envelopes are forming around each set.

explanation: In anaphase I the spindle separates the members of each homologous pair, so each pole receives one duplicated chromosome, and sister chromatids remain attached. B describes anaphase II, where the centromeres finally split. C invents a fourth pole, since a dividing cell has only two. D describes the events of telophase, not anaphase.
